reader_notes: Reads as authentic Swedish sakprosa of the popular-archaeology kind: concrete opening (spettet, motståndet som ändrar karaktär), then process, then a scholarly controversy, then an explicit 'det här vet vi inte' section, then a closing image. Paragraph function is clear throughout and I never had to reread a sentence to parse it.

Terminology is handled correctly and consistently: mossan (the moss) vs mossen (the bog) are kept apart; blästugn, lupp, räckning, varp, tappade kakor, rostbädd, tappgrop, mätts in are all real Swedish archaeometallurgical usage, and the four glossed terms are the ones a lay reader would actually need.

The metallurgy checks out: ~1200 grader melts the slag but not iron (which the text puts 'långt över 1500' - real value 1538); solid-state reduction with kolmonoxid drawing oxygen out of the ore grains; carburisation from harder blowing producing a more brittle bloom; low-iron (less fayalitic) slag being more viscous at bloomery temperatures. Nothing felt factually wrong to me.

Internal arithmetic hangs together across paragraphs: 'mer järn stannade i avfallet än som lämnade ugnen i luppen' is not asserted in a vacuum - it is corroborated later by 'en blåsning gav några kilo järn' against 'varpen räknas i ton'. Site counts are also consistent: 11 sampled furnace sites, 14 surveyed in the parish, 9 reconstructed furnaces, 36 firings.

Q1 (C): the passage says senhösten when the water had dropped, ore left out over the winter, 'Först därefter rostades den'. A inverts both season and order, B is contradicted by 'Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt', D by 'Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna'.

Q2 (A): 'De blåsningar som drevs hårdast ... gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet'. B reverses the direction, C overstates ('samtliga misslyckades'), D names something the experiments are never said to have shown.

Q3 (D): 'Det är hantverkets utgångspunkt ... Ur detta följer mycket' ties solid-state reduction to both the few-kilo bloom and the centre of gravity lying in the smithy. A contradicts the 300-1200s dating, B reverses which method needed vattenkraft, C contradicts 'uppteckningarna ... säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen'.

Q4 (B): the Tolvsater paragraph states the iron-rich slag was 'ett villkor' and that lower-iron slag turns viscous. A is Krokvall's reading, which the experiments are said to speak against; C is blocked by 'Krokvalls mätvärden har ingen ifrågasatt'; D is the strongest trap but the text explicitly refuses to explain the yield spread ('varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen').

Distractor set is honest: every wrong option is anchored to real text somewhere and falsified by a specific line, not by vagueness. No option was eliminable on length, register or hedging alone, and I could not have answered any of the four without reading the passage.
No cross-question leak. Q2 and Q4 both draw on the Tolvsater paragraph but on different findings (carburisation vs slag fluidity), and neither stem gives away the other's answer.

Two very small stylistic wobbles, neither of which slowed me down or affected an answer: 'Långt ifrån varje mosse' where 'Långt ifrån alla mossar' is the more common collocation, and 'en lera som sprack i fogarna' where a single moulded clay shaft does not obviously have 'fogar'. I would leave both as author's voice.

'vilket betyder att' in the Krokvall paragraph is a slightly strong connective - a third of the slag by weight only entails more iron lost than won given a slag:bloom mass ratio the reader has not yet been told. The later ton-vs-kilo contrast retroactively supports it, so this is a note about ordering, not an error.
